title: An end-point's two tokens, as the client receives them to return

source.note: composed: §6.2 ¶2 — an end-point receiving a token submessage "must include the same submessage with the exact same format, subformat and content in its response message to the peer end-point". The clause is symmetric, so this is a reply and the receiver is the client. The subformat suffix is §6.2.1's own example of one ('conversation_9.2.3.5', "to indicate that the message was created by the agent with identity 9.2.3.5"); the token contents are opaque to the protocol and are composed.

message.content: Ecma International is a standards organisation.

notes: `tokens` here is the set §6.2 ¶2 obliges the *receiver* to return, and this receiver is the client: the clause says "the end-point must include the same submessage with the exact same format, subformat and content in its response message", and a client's response is its next request. Both entries must come back with the subformat exactly as recorded — the `_srv-7` suffix is §6.2.1's identity of the agent that created the token, not decoration — and the second is not optional: §6.2.2 makes returning the authentication token unmodified an obligation, where §6.2.1's own token is only an invitation. The accessor for this in Rust is `Reply::tokens`, which is *not* this list alone: it chains `readings/36`'s first-submessage predicate in front of it, because a message that is itself a token carries one for §6.2's purposes. That composition is what no case here can pin, since `tokens` excludes the first submessage by definition. The two halves of it are asserted separately instead: `token_count` is two and `first_submessage_token` is explicitly none here, and `readings/36` is the message where the same two keys read one and a token.
